words.gloss: that which is to be feared

literal: Not fearing that which is to be feared is foolishness; fearing that which is to be feared is the action of those who know.
translation: Not to fear what ought to be feared is folly; to fear what ought to be feared is the way of the wise.
modern: அஞ்ச வேண்டியதற்கு அஞ்சாமல் இருப்பது அறியாமை ஆகும்; அஞ்ச வேண்டியதற்கு அஞ்சுவதே அறிவுடையோரின் செயலாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the relationship between wisdom and fear. It states that failing to fear things that genuinely deserve fear, such as moral evils or destructive dangers, is a sign of ignorance. True wisdom does not lie in blind, reckless courage. Instead, recognizing what is truly harmful and acting with a healthy, protective fear toward it is the characteristic behavior of those who possess knowledge.
